images.note: Box 1 muckrakers beat: Sinclair's The Jungle (1906) exposed Chicago meatpacking. Halftone from the 1906 book Chicago showing the Union Stock Yards with Packingtown in the distance — contemporary to the novel. Verified 2684x2238 JPEG. Alt: none — the LOC's 1906 Swift & Co. killing-hogs stereograph (item 2006679963) exists only as a TIFF master plus 150px thumb; TIFF transfers from tile.loc.gov break mid-download.
images.source: Internet Archive (scan of Chicago, L.H. Nelson Co., 1906; UIUC Open Content Alliance)

images.note: Box 1 muckrakers beat: Riis's How the Other Half Lives (1890). Primary is an actual Riis photograph ('One of four pedlars who slept in the cellar of 11 Ludlow Street rear', ca. 1890), verified 2600x1968 JPEG. Alt is the book's own 'Gotham Court' frontispiece — HONEST CAVEAT: visually confirmed it is an engraved illustration after Riis's photograph, not a photograph itself; included as the 1890 first edition's own visual argument.
images.source: Smithsonian American Art Museum (object 2016.40.6; gelatin silver print, printed ca. 1946 from ca. 1890 negative; Free to use)
images.title: Jacob Riis photograph: pedlars sleeping in a Ludlow Street cellar, ca. 1890

images.note: Box 1 settlement-house beat: Addams opened Hull House in 1889. Frontispiece portrait from her own 1910 memoir, captioned 'from a photograph taken in 1899' — contemporary to the Progressive Era. Verified 1650x2696 JPEG. Alt: none — LOC Addams portraits are TIFF-only; NPG's 1906 Brush portrait page is bot-blocked from this VM.
images.source: Internet Archive (scan of Twenty Years at Hull-House, first edition, 1910; University of Toronto copy)
images.title: Jane Addams, from a photograph taken in 1899 (frontispiece)
